item.title: Sabalenka edges Noskova in thriller to keep 3rd straight US Open title bid alive
item.description:
Aryna Sabalenka survived a dramatic battle against Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova on Tuesday, winning 7-6 (7-1), 3-6, 7-6 (10-7) to reach the US Open semifinals and keep her bid for a third consecutive title alive.
The world No. 1 was pushed to the limit by the sixth-seeded Czech before securing victory in a deciding-set match tiebreak.
Sabalenka will next face third-seeded Jessica Pegula, who came from a set down to defeat No. 26 Emma Navarro 3-6, 6-4, 6-3.
Sabalenka defeated Pegula in the 2024 US Open final and also beat her in last year's semifinals after losing the opening set.
The Belarusian sealed Tuesday's quarterfinal with an ace on her second serve, reaching the US Open semifinals for a sixth consecutive year.
Noskova came close to completing an impressive run after winning her maiden Grand Slam title at Wimbledon. She would have become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to follow a grass-court major title by reaching the US Open semifinals.
Sabalenka appeared close to an early exit when Noskova broke in the third set to move 4-2 ahead. But the top seed immediately responded, breaking back at love to level the set at 4-4.
The match went to a deciding tiebreak, where Noskova initially moved ahead 2-0. Sabalenka recovered after a double fault by Noskova gave her a 4-3 lead and then won the next two points to establish control.
Noskova finished with 46 winners and 18 aces, compared with Sabalenka's 42 winners and 12 aces.
Sabalenka had entered the tournament struggling for form on hard courts, losing in the fourth round in both Toronto and Cincinnati. She had also been eliminated at the same stage at Wimbledon.
However, she had not dropped a set before Tuesday's quarterfinal.
The result also kept alive Sabalenka's hopes of retaining the world No. 1 ranking, which she has held for 99 consecutive weeks.
She will lose the top spot if second-ranked Elena Rybakina defeats Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday to reach the semifinals. If Rybakina loses, Sabalenka can retain the ranking by winning the US Open title.
Tiafoe reaches men's semifinals
In the men's quarterfinals, No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe rallied from two sets down to defeat Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6).
Tiafoe will meet either defending champion Carlos Alcaraz or eighth-seeded Ben Shelton in the semifinals.
Their quarterfinal began shortly after 11 p.m. following a long day of matches.
Pegula rallies past Navarro
Pegula overcame a slow start against Navarro, who broke her twice in the opening set to take control.
But the third-seeded American recovered in the final stages, winning four consecutive games after Navarro had taken a 2-1 lead in the deciding set.
Pegula's victory set up another US Open meeting with Sabalenka, who will be seeking to maintain her dominance in New York.
For Noskova, the defeat ended her best-ever US Open campaign. Before this year, her best Grand Slam performance was a quarterfinal appearance at the 2024 Australian Open.

item.title: Khaled makes County debut as Hasan goes relentless
item.description:
Bangladesh pacer Khaled Ahmed made his debut in English County cricket today with Kent as his side took on Derbyshire in a crucial game at County Ground, Derby.
His compatriot Hasan Mahmud had already established his as main strike bowler of the Kent, setting a high bar for Bangladesh bowlers.
Hasan struck twice in the opening over against Derbyshire before Khaled messed with Derbyshire middle order on his very first match.
Hasan dismissed Harry Came and Matthew Montgomery in the first over, removing Came caught at slip before trapping Montgomery lbw with a delivery that came in sharply.
The two wickets took Hasan's county tally to 21, underlining his impressive form since making his Kent debut in June.
Hasan had announced himself in county cricket with nine wickets against Lancashire on debut, earning Player of the Match honors as Kent secured a 140-run victory. He added three wickets in his second match and later took seven wickets across two innings against Worcestershire to help Kent to another victory.
His county form came after an impressive Test performance for Bangladesh against Australia in Darwin last month, where he claimed nine wickets in the two innings, including six in the first innings, and was named Player of the Match. Khaled, meanwhile, made an immediate impact on his first appearance for Kent. The Bangladesh international claimed his maiden wicket in his fourth over, trapping Derbyshire opener Muhammad Naeem lbw.
He later dismissed Derbyshire captain Wayne Madsen for 29 to take his wickets tally to two as the opponent reached 122-4 in 39 overs.

item.title: Afghanistan to host multi-format series against Bangladesh and Zimbabwe
item.description:
Afghanistan will host both Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across October and November in an extensive multi-format programme in the United Arab Emirates, featuring a one-off Test, an ODI Tri-Nation Series involving all three sides, and a three-match T20I series and two-match Test series against Zimbabwe.
Proceedings begin with the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh from 9-13 October, before all three nations come together for the ODI Tri-Nation Series between 17 and 23 October.
Zimbabwe open their campaign against Bangladesh on 17 October, before facing hosts Afghanistan on 19 October. Afghanistan and Bangladesh then meet in the final league fixture on 21 October, with the top two sides progressing to the final on 23 October.
After the tri-series, Afghanistan and Zimbabwe switch to the shortest format for a three-match T20I series between 27 October and 1 November. The tour then concludes with a two-Test series between the two nations, running from 5-9 November and 13-17 November.
Afghanistan Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Naseeb Khan welcomed the confirmation of the schedule.
"We are pleased to confirm this important period of international cricket for the Afghanistan National Team," he said. "Playing Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across different formats will provide our players with valuable competitive opportunities and offer our supporters an exciting period of international cricket.
Bangladesh Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Nizam Uddin Chowdhury was similarly upbeat about the tour ahead, particularly the red-ball assignment.
"The Test match and the tri-nation series promise an exciting period of cricket for fans in both Bangladesh and Afghanistan," he said. "We attach great importance to Tests, and this will be an excellent opportunity for our players to experience red-ball cricket in the UAE for the first time and challenge themselves against a formidable Afghanistan side that has traditionally performed well in these conditions.
